anti_overlap: Does not re-derive whether specific Rust code sites (BenchTickContext defaults, HashMap sort/dedup order) are individually deterministic — takes the Rust-mechanism findings as given and asks whether the SCRIPT/GATE built on top would actually catch a violation of that mechanism.

Does not evaluate the data-generator/loader correctness (panic vs skip+warn, alias/353-count arithmetic, pillar-map coverage) at the data level — treats registry content as a given input to the referee/fog analysis.

Does not assess whether the pillar routing table's content is domain-correct (Infrastructure->tainter_complexity etc.) — only whether leaking routing data into the wrong visibility channel would matter.
decision_lens: For every comparison the referee or fog test performs, ask what a corrupted implementation would have to do to pass it anyway. If board construction touches anything shared with the refereed tick path, does the current strip-and-diff methodology actually detect that, or does it structurally blind itself to exactly the failure mode it claims to rule out? A gate whose scope excludes the actual site of concern provides zero real coverage no matter how reassuring its name.
focus: Whether the referee's flag-on/flag-off comparison logic and the fog-clean/grep gates actually constitute a valid, non-circular proof of world-inertness — or whether they can be satisfied by an implementation that still perturbs the world through a channel the comparison structurally cannot see.
name: fd-noninterference-proof-soundness
persona: Apply the perspective of a reviewer trained in information-flow/noninterference proofs and differential-testing methodology — someone who has debugged covert channels in deterministic replay systems and treats 'strip event X, diff the rest' as a necessary but not sufficient condition for non-interference: allocation patterns, RNG draw order, and timing can all leak through a trace that looks clean after naive event-stripping, and a grep-based gate proves absence only within the exact scope it searches.
review_areas: Assess whether 'flag-on trace minus issue_board events == flag-off trace' is logically sufficient to prove inertness, or whether it can pass despite board construction perturbing draw-order/timing/allocation that surfaces in OTHER (non-issue_board) event content — specifically whether IssueBoard::from_registry or issue_registry()'s OnceLock init touches any shared RNG, clock, or counter the refereed tick also consumes, and whether the base referee's norm() already neutralizes timestamp/ordering noise or leaves this exposed.

Verify the referee's reference comparison is well-chosen: is r2-a(flag-on,NEW)-minus-board vs r1-new(flag-off,NEW) the right pair, and is the pre-existing R1 OLD-vs-NEW byte-identity check preserved unweakened by adapting referee.sh into referee-issue-ingest.sh (did any assertion get dropped or altered in the copy)?

Check whether 'strip only event_type==issue_board' is complete — could the IssueBoard feature change the CONTENT (not just presence) of any other event type (a shifted tick counter, an extra roster stage, timestamp/ordering drift) that a whole-line-removal script wouldn't catch?

Evaluate acceptance criterion 5's git-grep world-inertness guard (scoped to emergence/ and runner_tick/) against the actual emit site the plan specifies in Task 5 (runner_bench.rs, NEITHER directory) — does the grep pass trivially by construction regardless of whether board data leaks into the tick path through some other identifier or indirection (a helper fn, a trait method, a closure capture)?

Evaluate the fog-clean test's banned-key list (reporter_honest, truthful, ground_truth, trend, visibility) for sufficiency against the actual HQ-visible ledger schema (recent_reports_json) — is the list drawn from the real leak surface or an assumed one, and would a genuinely leaking field (a raw score, an internal severity, a not-yet-coined name) slip past a fixed-string grep?

Determine whether the engagement guard (n_board >= 1) and the world-inert comparison could both report PASS under a subtly broken implementation simultaneously — i.e. is the combined PASS actually conjunctive-sufficient for the property claimed, or could each check individually pass while the combined property is violated?

severity_examples.condition: Lands in Acceptance Criterion 5 / breaks REFEREE gate's meaning (not its exit code) — the check as worded provides no actual coverage of the property it names.
severity_examples.scenario: Acceptance criterion 5's grep is scoped to crates/shadowbench-core/src/emergence/ and .../runner_tick/ only; the plan's own Task 5 places the ctx.issue_board read in runner_bench.rs, which is neither directory, so the grep reports zero hits — a trivial PASS — regardless of whether a future or sibling change adds a real tick-path read of issue_board somewhere else entirely outside those two directories.

severity_examples.condition: Lands in Task 6 (referee script) / breaks REFEREE gate silently — a false PASS on the world-inert leg.
severity_examples.scenario: If issue_registry()'s OnceLock::get_or_init(load) is first triggered mid-tick by build_issue_board_if_enabled() inside spawn_bench_loop, any allocator- or timing-sensitive downstream behavior could shift; strip_board only deletes issue_board lines, so a real perturbation surfacing as changed CONTENT in another event (not a new issue_board line) would not be caught by the world-inert comparison unless norm() already strips exactly the fields that would shift — this must be verified against the actual norm() implementation, not assumed.

severity_examples.condition: Lands in Task 5 Step 3 (fog-clean test) / breaks FOG gate's guarantee silently, not its exit code.
severity_examples.scenario: The fog-clean test's banned-key list is five strings chosen by the plan's author, not mechanically derived from the actual recent_reports_json schema; if that schema gains a field later (e.g. severity_score) the test gives permanent false assurance without ever being revisited.

success_hints: Reasons explicitly in terms of what a subtly-wrong implementation would have to do to still pass each gate — 'prove PASS is impossible under corruption X,' not just 'this could theoretically be wrong.'
Traces the actual file-scope of the acceptance-criterion-5 grep against the actual file Task 5 tells the executor to edit, rather than taking the criterion's stated intent at face value.

Flags any place where a 'prove' claim in the plan's own prose (Must-Haves, Task 6 comments) is not backed by an equally strong mechanical check, and suggests the minimal script edit or additional strip/assert needed to close the gap.

Correctly distinguishes an actual soundness gap from paranoia — if norm() (inherited from referee.sh) already handles a concern such as timestamp normalization, says so rather than re-flagging it as open.

For every finding, states which gate it breaks (REFEREE / FOG / DEMO) and the task#/criterion# per the task framing, and ranks by 'would ship a referee failure' vs 'would ship a silent world-perturbation.'
task_context: Adversarially review this execution-grade implementation plan (Phase 2 of the workipedia->emergence ingestion pipeline, shadowbench-core Rust crate) BEFORE weaker executors (sonnet subagents) build it literally. Core safety claim is WORLD-INERTNESS: a new IssueBoard lives on BenchTickContext (bench-only, cfg(feature=bench)), built once at spawn_bench_loop, EMPTY when the SHADOWBENCH_ISSUE_INGEST env flag is off (empty-when-off discipline copied from cadre/bench_history), surfaced ONLY as a flag-on-only TraceEvent::IssueBoard that NEVER writes the chronicle. The divergence referee (scripts/bench/divergence/referee-issue-ingest.sh) must prove: R1 flag-off byte-identical OLD-vs-NEW (chronicle sha + normalized trace), flag-on chronicle byte-identical to flag-off, and flag-on-trace-minus-issue_board-events == flag-off trace (world-inert), plus a board-engaged guard. Hunt hardest for, and name where each lands (task#/criterion#) + whether it breaks the REFEREE gate, FOG gate, or DEMO + minimal fix: (1) any path where plan code perturbs the FLAG-OFF world and breaks R1 byte-identity — a BenchTickContext construction site not defaulting issue_board, adding a struct field/enum variant that changes serialization/hashing of EXISTING artifacts, a non-deterministic board build (IssueRegistry is a HashMap; board sorts by id — verify airtight), or OnceLock registry init on the flag-off path with an observable side effect. (2) Is the world-inert PROOF valid or circular: does 'flag-on trace minus issue_board == flag-off trace' truly prove inertness, or could board construction (registry OnceLock init, allocations, RNG touch) shift draw-count/draw-order or timing that leaks into the trace even with board events stripped? Is r2-a(flag-on,NEW)-minus-board vs r1-new(flag-off,NEW) the right reference, and is the existing referee's OLD-vs-NEW R1 preserved? Does stripping only event_type==issue_board suffice if the feature changes any other event? (3) Loader correctness: panic-on-invalid (Rust) vs skip+warn (Python generator) mismatch — could committed JSON contain a row the loader rejects? Alias handling + the 353-distinct-count assertion vs alias keys inflating HashMap len. Pillar-map must cover all 16 labels or the loader panics at runtime — guaranteed? Generated-JSON staleness --check guard; include_str! of a stale committed file. (4) Fog parity: is the board truly eval/scorer-side, or could a step leak it into the HQ-visible ledger (recent_reports_json) or agent-visible state? The fog-clean test greps a fixed banned-key list — sufficient? (5) Demo reachability: will 'ai-alignment-crisis' appear in a TICKS=200 flag-on run given the board emits at the initial-roster (BenchStarted) site — is that site reached, is --inline-strategy random correct, referee SEED/TICKS (1000/8766) consistency? (7) Routing choices (Infrastructure->tainter_complexity, Technology->compute, Human Capital->[labor,demographics], Rival Orgs->intelligence, Health->demographics, all approximate) — any mis-route that misleads eval/player; do pillar name strings that don't resolve to real modules matter given Phase 2 doesn't invoke pillars? Rank by whether a literal executor would ship a referee failure or a silent world-perturbation; findings that would over-build the plan should say so and propose trimming. Within this task, your specific lane is the PROOF/GATE logic itself — the referee script's comparison structure, the grep-based world-inertness check, and the fog-clean banned-key list — asking whether each actually detects the violation it claims to, not whether the underlying Rust mechanism or the corpus data is individually correct (those are the other two reviewers' lanes).
